description: Notes from the human editor directing the curmudgeon to review specific items with specific focus areas. Check at the start of every run. Pending notes take priority over the normal tracker sequence. Mark notes as consumed after reviewing.

notes.topic: WIN-010 cycle 18: narrow deep-attack review of EXP-684-rev2 (c17 fixes plus the new BOU 2017 Z evidence), before integration
notes.context: WIN-010.c17 (q609) approved EXP-684 rev1 subject to sentence-level fixes (ISS-3110 Chapman 1933 mis-citation, ISS-3111 batch). The analyst's rev2 (2026-09-29) goes beyond those fixes. To source the amplitude (c17 hole 1), it adds Meza et al. 2022 and its own INTERMAGNET-definitive computation. Together these show BOU Z was NOT depressed at the 2017 eclipse relative to quiet days (+0.8 nT at 17:20, +4.9 nT at maximum), and that the dome's -18.22 nT is matched by ordinary quiet days (-9.3 to -27.3 nT). That is a new evidential argument in a verdict-bearing panel, so it must not integrate unreviewed. This note commissions the cycle directly. No decider queue push is needed.
scope_artifacts: monitor/analyst/analysis-records/win010-c17-rev2-verification-20260929.json - BOU Z check + DE440s, scripts and checksums
notes.mechanism: Single operator-commission review, cycle 18, deep-attack, narrow scope. Takes priority over the normal queue this run. Write reviews/WIN-010.c18.json.
review_focus_hints: (i) Attack the BOU Z computation from BOTH sides. Check the quiet-day selection, the baseline definition, the timing (local vs UT), and INTERMAGNET vs USGS data (USGS returns Z=99999 for Aug 2017). Did we pick a reference that happens to erase the dome's number? Would a reasonable alternative reference reproduce the dome's -10.9 / -18.22 nT as an eclipse effect?

(ii) Check the Meza et al. 2022 reading against the paper itself. Confirm authors, title, DOI and that it says dZ at BOU was small and positive with the signal mainly in dX. We have had three citation failures in this cluster (Kim & Chang 2018, the Hartland 'NASA calculation', Chapman 1933); do not accept a citation on the analyst's paraphrase.

(iii) Answer the verdict question: 'Std Model Explains' vs 'Refuted by Data'. If the dome's specific observed number is a baseline artefact, is 'Std Model Explains' now too generous to the dome, or too harsh to it? Whichever you pick, give the rule so it can be applied symmetrically to our own claims.
(iv) Spot-verify the c17 hole 0-10 fixes, especially hole 0 (Chapman 1933 now described as a theoretical expectation that the observations of the time did not show) and the AACGM latitude numbers.

(v) Public-date text must read 2026-10-31. The post-event paragraph must say plainly that our binary profile failed (per c3 C3-3), OR state that the post-event result waits for EXP-687. It must not read as though the pre-event expectation held.

notes.topic: Cycle-4 frozen-prediction review (deep-attack) of the eclipse 2026-08-12 MAGNETIC-bucket results draft rev4 (EXP-687-rev4), before any verdict integration or OTS stamp
notes.context: Cycle 3 (reviews/ECLIPSE-2026-08-12-MAGNETIC-RESULTS-proposal.c3.json) returned REVISE (targeted, rev4): C3-1 critical, C3-2..C3-4 major, plus moderates and minors (ISS-3106..3109). It also folds in HNOTE-ANALYST-EXP687-REV4-SIDEFINDINGS-2026-09-30: position-dependent dZ sign, H vs Z per registration, INTERMAGNET data, x1.672 applied once. This note commissions cycle 4 directly. If HNOTE-OPERATOR-WIN010-C18-EXP684REV2-2026-09-30 is still pending, do that one first (older) and this one on the next run.
notes.mechanism: Single targeted operator-commission review (cycle 4, deep-attack, requires_frozen_prediction_review). Verify closure of C3-1..C3-13. Apply 'Frozen-Prediction Reviews: Attack Our Side Too'. Write reviews/ECLIPSE-2026-08-12-MAGNETIC-RESULTS-proposal.c4.json with a recommendation (publish-ready / minor_edit / REVISE). Do not assign verdicts.
review_focus_hints: NEW decision_5 (PRED-095 registration): rev4 says the dome's PRED-095 CARD (-17.8 +/-2 nT at EBR/SPT, falsified by H within +/-3 nT of 0) scored on H is NEITHER confirmed NOR falsified (raw H -9.6 / -12.6 nT). It also says our predictions.json PRED-095 claim text merged the card with the dome's Z 'revised prediction' paragraph, which is our representation error. Check this against the dome's own predictions.html text at the pinned commit. Is recommending 'score the card' principled, or does it pick the registration that avoids a verdict? Apply the same rule we would want applied to our B1-M-001.

C3-2: verify the control-day calibration that widened the joint-fit uncertainty (WLS se ~2.3x too small). Check that the x1.672 spec is rejected and the -10.9 baseline only disfavoured in every variant. Check the same calibration was applied to our side's fits.

Position-dependent dZ sign: check rev4 applied it to the dome Tier-1 template AND to our B1-M-001 sign convention. Check that 'standard physics' is represented with the sign geometry (Ashour-Chapman thin sheet / Meza 2022), not a one-signed minimum. Verify the Meza 2022 citation directly (authors, title, DOI, what it says about BOU dZ). Do not accept the paraphrase; three citation failures in this cluster so far.

WIN-010 profile: rev4 says our binary profile FAILED; the latitude-ordered residual has no established cause; FSF fits only modestly better than flat; solar-elevation fits as well or better. Check this is stated in the headline, as plainly as a dome failure would be.
Withdrawn claims ('mostly curvature'; 'any summer day'): check they are withdrawn everywhere, including the headline and proposed public notes, not just in the hole table.

Reproducibility: every input is hashed and 4 rev3 outputs reproduce byte-identically. Spot-check at least one end to end. Note that 2026 INTERMAGNET definitive data are not yet published: is scoring on quasi-definitive/provisional data acceptable for an OTS-stamped results file, or should the stamp wait?
Operator decision on archiving inputs under predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-results-inputs/ before the stamp: give a recommendation.
